comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum explicitly applies to the 2026 entrant cohort and fixes the programme at 180 EC: a 127.5-EC major and 52.5 EC of profiling space. The major comprises two first-year foundation packages (eight courses, 60 EC); six 7.5-EC depth courses (45 EC); one 7.5-EC methods course; a 7.5-EC professional, creative and academic writing course preparing the capstone; and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis. A Fall-2026 entrant reaches Year 2 in 2027-2028 and therefore follows the odd-year Trans-Atlantic Perspectives package (Competencias de lectura y conciencia cultural, Migration and Diaspora, Testimonios/crónicas/imágenes, and Variation and Change in Language). In Year 3, the student takes two courses from the even-year package; the first two officially listed courses, Lengua, cultura e identidad and Contesting the Past, are selected neutrally. Research Methods Intercultural Communication is the first-listed eligible methods choice. The current official page identifies Crossing Borders as an optional alternative track; the standard Trans-Atlantic Perspectives package best represents the generic normalized target's Spanish-language-and-culture identity and is selected before UCR fit is considered. The genuine 52.5-EC profiling space remains open. The resulting pathway accounts for exactly 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized target does not name the optional Crossing Borders track. The standard Trans-Atlantic Perspectives package most directly represents the programme's Spanish-language, Spanish and Latin American identity. The odd-year package applies when a Fall-2026 entrant reaches Year 2; two first-listed even-year courses complete the required six-course depth sequence in Year 3. The first-listed methods option breaks the remaining neutral tie. All selections were fixed before UCR fit was considered.

exception.reason: Utrecht's programme is defined by a compulsory four-course Spanish-language acquisition sequence progressing from CEFR A1 to B2, followed by Spanish-medium and Spanish-specific study of sociolinguistics, morphosyntax, language change, intercultural communication, Spanish and Latin American literature, theatre, film, migration, colonial chronicles, cultural identity and historical memory. UCR's current curriculum contains no Spanish-language course and no course whose disciplinary object is Spanish language, Hispanic linguistics, Spanish or Latin American literature, or the cultures of Spain and Latin America. UCR literature, media, history, sociology and communication courses can illuminate isolated comparative themes, but they cannot supply the language competence on which the comparator's advanced courses and thesis depend. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a broad literature, media and cultural-studies programme without Spanish, not a defensible closest match to Spanish Language and Culture.
exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026-entry curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: a 127.5-EC major and 52.5 EC of profiling space. The major contains 60 EC of compulsory first-year foundations, including 30 EC of progressive Spanish acquisition; 45 EC of Trans-Atlantic Perspectives depth study; a 7.5-EC methods course; a 7.5-EC professional/creative/academic writing course; and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis. The standard Trans-Atlantic pathway is selected for the generic programme, while the optional Crossing Borders track is not combined with it. Genuine profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor or electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches Spanish language at any level, Spanish linguistics, Hispanic literature, or Spanish and Latin American cultural history as its sustained disciplinary object. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literature, MCCLITR112 Texts & Worlds, MCCLITR212 Literature & Society, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Contemporary Literatures offer transferable literary and cultural analysis; MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI211 Media Archaeology, MCCCOMM211 Intercultural Communication and MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication offer adjacent media and communication study; GOSHIST courses provide broad historical methods and selected regional themes; and GOSSOCI212 provides qualitative research. These courses could support comparative cultural work, but none develops Spanish speaking, listening, reading or writing, and none supports progression from A1 to B2 or prepares students to conduct advanced Spanish-language coursework and an independent thesis in the field. Because the missing language sequence is a prerequisite academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent Spanish Language and Culture programme.
